text:
samira: quick heads-up from the dedicated int8 onboarding (kestrel-int8). we're seeing a low-rate class of funcall failures that don't match previous patterns. ~7/1000 invokes get flagged as 'schema: missing actions' but raw captures are inconsistent: sometimes top-level array, sometimes duplicated trailing tokens, and once we saw a stray comma at the very front. looks like assembly-level noise rather than model hallucination. :thinking_face:

otto: can you paste a sanitized raw for one of each class? helps decide whether it's truncation, duplication, or accidental token insertion.

samira: pasted three sanitized examples (redacted ids):
```json
// A - top-level array
[
  {"tool":"create_note","params":{"text":"deploy done"}}
]

// B - duplicated trailing bracket
{"actions":[{"tool":"close_ticket","params":{"id":9001}}]}]

// C - leading comma then object
, {"actions":[{"tool":"remind","params":{"when":"tomorrow"}}]}
```

lucas: fp16 baseline clean. correlation: kvcache=prefix + streaming mode=segmented + batch >=6 increases rate. Also most fails land exactly at chunk boundary in assembler_trace. replay-bot: can you run a double replay (kvcache on/off) over the failing seed set and capture assembler_trace + token_hex + kernel_pick?

replay-bot: replay started: job_id=rj-4412 seeds=2500 model=kestrel-int8 nodes=2 batch=8. artifacts: https://ci.internal/canary/rj-4412 :rocket:

otto: if artifacts show chunk boundary alignment with corrupted bytes that's an assembler reassembly bug. but duplicated "]" suggests chunk duplication on splice, and leading comma hints at an off-by-one where a previous chunk's trailing comma gets left dangling. two levers: (1) quick mitigation = postproc normalizer (strip leading commas, dedupe adjacent identical terminators, wrap top-level array into {"actions": ...}) and treat as retryable, (2) root cause = patch stream_assembler to recompute offsets after prefix splicing and enforce no duplicate append.

samira: i'm pushing the postproc normalizer as an emergency patch on the canary branch and bumping retry_policy to linear-2. will keep kvcache disabled for segmented streaming in the broader rollout until we validate.

lucas: can you also capture raw token ids around the splice? if the token ids themselves contain comma or bracket tokens twice, that might be tokenization jitter; if token ids line up but bytes duplicated, assembler likely doing a memcpy twice.

replay-bot: first replay summary: kvcache=on segmented=on => 7.1/1000 parse_fail; kvcache=off segmented=on => 0.8/1000; segmented=off kvcache=on => 0.9/1000. 73% of fails end exactly at chunk refill boundary. token_hex + assembler_trace attached.

otto: that strongly points to reassembler churn when cached prefixes are spliced in. lucas, please open infra ticket with chunk_map + assembler_trace + kernel_pick for the failing requests. i'll put up a minimal unit-test for chunk_splice that simulates cached prefix insertion and asserts no duplicated bytes.

samira: for customer safety we keep postproc normalizer and sentinel injection (append <ACTIONS_END> if missing) on the canary cluster. will mark heuristic_wrap metric so we can track. also adding an alert if heuristic_wrap > 1/1000 over 10m window.

lucas: PR coming to recompute total_length after joining chunks and to assert final byte is one of '}', ']' before handing to parser. also adding a small defensive retry in assembler: if final byte invalid, attempt a refill window read of up to 128 bytes before failing.

replay-bot: updated replay: after postproc+sentinel, effective parse_fail reduced to 0.6/1000 on the canary. will re-run with new assembler patch once it lands.

otto: once assembler PR lands, let's run seeded compare across kernel variants (packed-attn vs stable-attn) to rule out kernel selection interaction. if stable-attn reduces fails even with kvcache enabled that suggests a timing/latency-induced boundary race in the fast kernels.

samira: agreed. plan: 1) keep postproc normalizer & sentinel in canary, 2) land assembler dedupe+assert+refill patch behind a kill-switch, 3) run seeded replays across kernel picks and batch sizes, 4) re-enable kvcache segmented flows gradually if green. i'll post the ticket links and results here. thanks all. :rocket:
